les: Iemand om na op te kyk
kaps_punt: Weeklikse lees deur leerders: lees vir genot: Lees oor rolmodelle of suksesvolle mense/mense met selfvertroue.

items.bewering: Siya Kolisi het as klein seun op 'n growwe veld in Zwide rugby gespeel.
items.bron: Sunday Times, 2 Feb 2020, 'Siya Kolisi creates field of dreams for township kids' (sundaytimes.timeslive.co.za): as a child he played barefoot on grassless fields; his early ground is described as a thorny, gravel-strewn field in Zwide.

items.bewering: Zwide is 'n township in die stad wat ons vandag Gqeberha noem.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Siya Kolisi' (Zwide, iBhayi, a township in Port Elizabeth); SA History Online, 'Siyamthanda Kolisi' (Zwide Township in Port Elizabeth); Port Elizabeth renamed Gqeberha in the Government Gazette of 23 Feb 2021 (TimesLIVE / The Herald, 23 Feb 2021; SAnews 'Name change shakeup for the Eastern Cape').

items.bewering: Hy is in 1991 daar gebore
items.bron: SA History Online, 'Siyamthanda Kolisi': born 16 June 1991 in Zwide Township in Port Elizabeth. Wikipedia infobox: 16 June 1991, Port Elizabeth.

items.bewering: en het by sy ouma grootgeword.
items.bron: SA History Online: raised by his paternal grandmother. The Citizen, 'LONG READ: The incredible journey of Siya Kolisi': grew up with his grandmother, aunt and uncle in Zwide. (Sources differ on when the grandmother died, at about 9 to 12, after which an aunt raised him; the lesson makes no claim about that, so nothing turns on it.)

items.bewering: Daar was dikwels min kos in die huis
items.bron: Sunday Times, 3 Oct 2021, Kolisi: 'When there was no food in our house, I would hang out at the neighbours' places and ask for food'; CNN (via abc17news.com, 17 Jan 2022): finding enough to eat was a daily struggle; The Citizen long read: 'Going hungry was hardly a weird feeling.'

items.bewering: en geen geld vir rugbyskoene nie.
items.bron: Sports Illustrated interview, 6 May 2020: 'Going to school without shoes on - we couldn't afford that sometimes'; Sunday Times, 2 Feb 2020: he played barefoot as a child. No source states the words 'no money for rugby boots', but a household that sometimes could not afford school shoes, and a boy who played barefoot, support it. Bryan Habana (The Citizen, via PressReader, 2 Nov 2019) contrasts worrying about boots with worrying about food.

items.bewering: Party aande was daar niks om te eet nie, en hy het honger gaan slaap.
items.bron: Sports Illustrated, 6 May 2020, Kolisi: 'Going to bed without food in my stomach, that is one thing I feel like I don't wish on anybody'; CNN 2022: he sometimes went a couple of days without eating.

items.bewering: Siya het by African Bombers, 'n klub in sy eie buurt, leer rugby speel.
items.bron: SA History Online: started rugby at seven and joined the local African Bombers Rugby Club; Kolisi's own account (SA Rugby Mag) puts the club at Dan Qeqe Stadium, a few streets from his house.

items.bewering: Hy het as kind dikwels kaalvoet gespeel.
items.bron: Sunday Times, 2 Feb 2020: he played barefoot on grassless fields as a child. Rachel Kolisi (YOU, 14 June 2018, via PressReader, as quoted in search results) said he went barefoot for his first ten years.

items.bewering: Hy is later vir die provinsie se onder-twaalfspan gekies. Daardie span het by 'n groot toernooi in Mosselbaai gaan speel.
items.bron: The Citizen, 'LONG READ: The incredible journey of Siya Kolisi': 'picked for Eastern Province's Under-12 B side for a provincial tournament in Mossel Bay'. Wikipedia and Nelson Mandela University (Council award 2018): at 12 he impressed scouts at a youth tournament in Mossel Bay. Note for the writer, not a fault: it was the province's under-12 B side. 'Die provinsie se onder-twaalfspan' is not false, but if precision is wanted, 'n onder-twaalfspan van die provinsie' fits the source more closely.

items.bewering: Siya het daar goed gespeel. Daarna het Grey Junior, 'n skool in die stad, vir hom 'n beurs aangebied.
items.bron: Nelson Mandela University, 'Siya Kolisi 2018': 'at age 12, he impressed talent scouts at a youth rugby tournament in Mossel Bay' and 'was offered a scholarship at Grey Junior in Port Elizabeth'; same in Wikipedia and SA History Online. The Citizen and a 2017 Daily Dispatch piece name Grey High for the bursary, but Wikipedia records both: a scholarship to Grey Junior, then a rugby scholarship to Grey High. So the sources are not in conflict.

items.bewering: In sy nuwe klas het almal Engels gepraat, en hy het min daarvan verstaan. Hy moes die taal van die begin af leer en het aangehou rugby speel.
items.bron: SA History Online: 'Upon his arrival at Grey Junior, he could not speak a word of English'; a classmate, Nicholas Holton, taught him English. Sports Illustrated 2020, Kolisi: 'I couldn't speak a word of English' and had to learn 'from ABCD'. The Grey schools teach in English (Grey High School, Wikipedia and school descriptions), which supports 'almal Engels gepraat' in class.

items.bewering: Sy ma is oorlede terwyl hy nog op skool was.
items.bron: Wikipedia (early life), The Citizen and Sports Illustrated: his mother died when he was 15. SA History Online says 16, and Wikipedia's family section gives 2009, when he would have been about 18 and in his final school year (he went to the Western Province Rugby Institute in 2010). The sources disagree on the exact age, but every version falls during his school years, which is all the lesson claims.

items.bewering: Ná skool het hy vir 'n groot span in Kaapstad begin speel.
items.bron: SA History Online: arrived at the Western Province Rugby Institute in Stellenbosch in 2010 and made his Stormers debut in 2012; Wikipedia: Western Province senior debut in the 2011 Vodacom Cup, joined the Stormers squad in 2012. Both teams are Cape Town sides (Newlands).

items.bewering: In 2013 het hy sy eerste toetswedstryd vir die Springbokke gespeel.
items.bron: Wikipedia: Test debut on 15 June 2013 against Scotland in Nelspruit, 30-17 win; SA History Online: Test debut in 2013 against Scotland in Nelspruit.

items.bewering: Toe hy drie-en-twintig was, het hy sy jonger suster en broer by hom ingeneem.
items.bron: The Irish Mail on Sunday, 3 June 2018 (via PressReader): 'aged 23, became their legal guardian'; The Citizen long read: 'Kolisi was 23' when he found his half-siblings Liyema and Liphelo and then sought legal guardianship; Wikipedia: they have lived in the Kolisi household since 2014 (he turned 23 in June 2014). Both are younger half-siblings.

items.bewering: In 2018 het die afrigter hom as kaptein van die Springbokke aangewys.
items.bron: Wikipedia: named Springbok captain in May 2018; The Citizen long read: coach Rassie Erasmus confirmed him as captain for the Test series against England, in front of the squad of 43.

items.bewering: Hy was die eerste swart speler wat die span in 'n toetswedstryd gelei het.
items.bron: Wikipedia: named captain in May 2018, 'becoming the first black man to hold the position', the first black captain 'in its 126-year history'; SA History Online: 'the first black player to captain the Springboks'; The Citizen: 'the first black man to be bestowed the honour'. The lesson's version, limited to a Test match, is the careful form and is supported.

items.bewering: In 2019 het hy sy knie lelik beseer. Die Wêreldbeker in Japan sou net 'n paar maande later begin.
items.bron: TimesLIVE, 30 May 2019, 'Injured Siya Kolisi in race against time to be fit for Boks': a knee injury against the Highlanders in May 2019 ended his Super Rugby season and put his World Cup build-up at risk; he wore a brace for six weeks instead of having surgery. SA Rugby Mag: 'knee ligament injury while playing Super Rugby for the Stormers'. The 2019 World Cup opened on 20 September 2019, about four months later.

items.bewering: Siya het week ná week gewerk om weer behoorlik te kan hardloop. Hy het betyds herstel en die span Japan toe gelei.
items.bron: TimesLIVE 30 May 2019 (six weeks in a brace instead of surgery, then rehabilitation); Daily Maverick 30 Apr 2023 (the non-surgical route 'proved to be the right decision, as Kolisi made it to Japan'); SA Rugby Mag (recovered to play warm-ups against Argentina and Japan); Wikipedia (captained South Africa at the 2019 World Cup).

items.bewering: Die Springbokke het die eerste wedstryd teen Nieu-Seeland verloor.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 8 Oct 2019, 'Boks thrash Canada to confirm quarter-final place': lost the pool opener 23-13 to New Zealand.

items.bewering: Daarna het Suid-Afrika elke wedstryd gewen en tot in die eindstryd deurgedring. Daar het hulle Engeland geklop.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 8 Oct 2019: after the New Zealand loss they beat Namibia 57-3, Italy 49-3 and Canada 66-7; Daily Maverick, 20 Oct 2019, and ESPN: beat Japan 26-3 in the quarter-final; world.rugby and ESPN: beat Wales 19-16 in the semi-final; Wikipedia: beat England 32-12 in the final in Yokohama. Wikipedia 'South Africa at the Rugby World Cup': 2019, 7 played, 6 won, 1 lost. 'Elke wedstryd' after the opener holds.

items.bewering: Siya het as kaptein die goue beker bo sy kop gelig.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Siya Kolisi': captained South Africa to the 2019 title. Wikipedia 'Webb Ellis Cup' and rugby365 'The Webb Ellis Cup': the trophy is gilded silver, so it looks gold. 'Goue' reads correctly as its colour. It is not solid gold, which matters only if a later text says it is made of gold.

items.bewering: Die span het daarna met die beker na groot stede getoer.
items.bron: SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/45735), 6 Nov 2019, 'See your Springbok heroes on the Champions Tour': Pretoria, Johannesburg, Soweto, Durban, East London, Port Elizabeth, ending in Cape Town on 11 November 2019.

items.bewering: 'n Oop bus met die beker het stadig deur Zwide se strate gery. Siya het die beker terug na die buurt van sy kinderdae gebring.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 10 Nov 2019, 'Huge turnout for Kolisi as Boks bring Webb Ellis Cup home to PE': the bus ran along Spondo and Koyana/Konyana roads in Zwide, 'could hardly move in Koyana Street as thousands of Zwide residents lined the streets', Kolisi 'stood on the bus' holding the trophy and 'brought the trophy home'. SAnews 'Taste of victory' (7 Nov 2019) confirms the tour used an open-top bus.

items.bewering: Hy het kort daarna 'n stigting begin wat gesinne met kos help.
items.bron: Kolisi Foundation (kolisifoundation.org, 'Kolisi Foundation - What's in store for 2021?'): launched in April 2020 as South Africa entered lockdown, about five months after the November 2019 tour; started with food parcels and vouchers, more than 32 800 food parcels in 2020, much of it in Zwide. CNN 2022: launch brought forward; food parcels to Zwide. Wikipedia: food insecurity is one of its focus areas. It was co-founded with his wife Rachel, and 'hy het ... begin' does not deny that.

items.bewering: In 2023 het die Springbokke weer om die Wêreldbeker gespeel. Die eindstryd was in Frankryk, en hulle het dit gewen.
items.bron: World Rugby, 'Rugby World Cup 2023 finals review', and Planet Rugby: South Africa beat New Zealand 12-11 in the final at the Stade de France (Saint-Denis, Paris) on 28 October 2023.

items.bewering: Siya het die goue beker daar vir die tweede keer bo sy kop gelig.
items.bron: World Rugby 2023 finals review: Kolisi became the second captain to lift the Webb Ellis Cup twice; Wikipedia: captained the 2019 and 2023 winning sides.

items.bewering: beurs: Geld wat iemand anders vir jou skool of studie betaal.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'bursary': 'an amount of money that is given to somebody so that they can study'; Britannica Dictionary, 'bursary': money a student is given to help pay for study. Kolisi's Grey award was a full bursary covering school costs (The Citizen), so 'skool of studie' fits the story's use. The entry holds when read alone.

items.bewering: toetswedstryd: 'n Groot wedstryd tussen die nasionale spanne van twee lande.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'test match': a cricket or rugby match played between the teams of two different countries; Wikipedia 'Test match (rugby union)': an international match, usually between two senior national teams. Rare exceptions such as the British and Irish Lions do not make the Grade 4 wording false.

items.bewering: eindstryd: Die laaste wedstryd van 'n toernooi, tussen die twee spanne wat die wedstryde net daarvoor gewen het.
items.bron: This is how a knockout final works, as in the story: in 2019 South Africa reached the final by beating Wales in the semi-final, and England by beating New Zealand; the final was the tournament's last match (world.rugby; ESPN; rugby365 RWC results). The entry is true of the knockout tournaments the lesson is about.

items.bewering: stigting: 'n Groep wat geld insamel om ander mense te help.
items.bron: Philanthropy Impact glossary, 'foundation': a foundation is typically a trust whose income comes from an endowment of land or invested capital, and not all foundations make grants; American Heritage (via YourDictionary/Dictionary.com): 'an organization established to maintain, assist, or finance institutions or projects of a social, educational, charitable, religious' nature; Vocabulary.com: 'an institution supported by an endowment'. A glossary entry is read on its own, and this one makes fundraising the thing that makes something a foundation. Many foundations work with money they were given or already hold and raise none. The help-others part is true of the charitable foundations the story means. Kolisi's foundation does raise money, so the story itself is not wrong.
items.regstelling: Define a stigting by what it is for, not by fundraising: an organisation set up to use money for a good purpose, such as helping people. Raising money may be mentioned as something many foundations do, but not as the defining feature. For example: "'n Organisasie wat geld gebruik om 'n goeie doel te dien, soos om mense te help." Use 'organisasie' or 'instelling' rather than 'groep'.

opsomming: Every biographical claim about Siya Kolisi, including the one superlative, is confirmed by South African and rugby sources, and the only fault is the glossary entry for 'stigting', which wrongly makes fundraising what defines a foundation and should define it by its purpose instead.
